Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-16x & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({y}^{2}-16x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({y}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(16x) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(16x) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2y)-\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot 16 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=\frac{1}{4},$ $x=1,$ and $y=4,$ and solving for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2y)-\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot 16 & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2\cdot 4)-(\frac{1}{4})\cdot 16 & =0 \\ 8\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-4 & =0 \\ 8\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =4 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
